proposed_comments.title: Honor no-cycle navigation consistently across modes and monitors
proposed_comments.body:
### Honor no-cycle navigation consistently across modes and monitors

**Severity:** `high`

The new setting must control both position-based and zone-index keyboard navigation. With cycling disabled, movement should still reach an adjacent monitor when one exists, then stop without wrapping at the global edge; the native and Settings defaults must also agree so an untouched configuration behaves consistently. Please wire the value through native settings parsing, UI serialization, and both navigation paths rather than applying the early exit only to one helper.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve navigation, snap failures, and native window-state sequencing
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve navigation, snap failures, and native window-state sequencing

**Severity:** `high`

Win+Up/Down should maximize or minimize only when there is genuinely no directional zone target. An unsnapped or intermediate-zone window must navigate first, the first Win+Down on a maximized window must restore it, and a real `WorkArea::Snap` failure must be returned instead of being reinterpreted as a boundary. Please keep a distinct no-target result, initialize `WINDOWPLACEMENT.length`, and use asynchronous placement for HWNDs owned by another thread so the expected maximize → restore → navigate → minimize sequence is preserved.

proposed_comments.title: Persist the setting and keep native/UI defaults aligned
proposed_comments.body:
### Persist the setting and keep native/UI defaults aligned

**Severity:** `medium`

The Settings toggle must update the repository, send the IPC payload, survive serialization with a non-default value, and match the native default before any settings file exists. Please keep the resource text localizable and include the new value in the existing FancyZones settings telemetry so configuration and runtime behavior do not silently diverge.

proposed_comments.title: Add deterministic boundary and persistence regression coverage
proposed_comments.body:
### Add deterministic boundary and persistence regression coverage

**Severity:** `medium`

Please cover cycling-disabled navigation in both index and position modes, single- and multi-monitor transitions, global edges, unsnapped windows, and maximize/restore/minimize state changes. Add Settings tests that prove the toggle persists and native serialization tests for `cycle-through-zones=false`; keep mock-window placement deterministic and reset singleton settings between cases so teardown or test order cannot mask regressions.

prs.testInstructions: Launch <PowerToysCheckout>\x64\Debug\PowerToys.exe, disable zone cycling in FancyZones settings, and verify adjacent-monitor movement, global-edge stopping, and maximize/restore/minimize sequencing.

tests.detail: Snap_Down depends on the default position of a mock HWND and currently selected a different artificial monitor; an earlier run passed 16/16. This is separate from the deterministic disabled-cycle edge cases, which pass.
VSTest can exit with access violation -1073741819 during mock-window teardown, sometimes before printing the summary. Targeted suites return clean success.

verification.localBuildNote: The machine lacks Spectre libraries. The documented conditional POWERTOYS_DISABLE_SPECTRE property overrides were applied only for local validation, restored afterward, and never committed or pushed.

test_instructions: Open Settings → FancyZones → Window behavior, toggle the new zone-cycling option off, restart PowerToys, and confirm the value persists.
With Override Windows Snap enabled, move a window through zones with Win+Left/Right and Win+Up/Down. Confirm it can cross to an adjacent monitor but stops without wrapping at the global edge.
From an unsnapped or intermediate-zone window, press Win+Up/Down and confirm it navigates to the next zone before maximizing or minimizing.
Maximize a zoned window, then press Win+Down repeatedly. Confirm the first press restores, subsequent presses navigate downward, and only the true bottom boundary minimizes.
